title: Implement the three depth-first traversals of a binary tree: inorder, preorder, and postorder: both recursively and iteratively using an explicit stack.
shortTitle: Binary Tree Inorder/Preorder/Postorder: recursive and iterative (stack)
keyPoints: Preorder is node-left-right, inorder is left-node-right, postorder is left-right-node.
Recursive forms are direct translations of the definitions with a null base case.
Iterative forms replace the call stack with an explicit ArrayDeque stack to avoid StackOverflowError on tall trees.
Iterative preorder: push root, pop-visit-push right then left so left is processed first.
Iterative inorder: go left pushing nodes, then pop-visit-go right.
Inorder traversal of a BST yields sorted order, making it the natural choice for BST problems.

s1_definition.oneliner: Preorder is node-left-right, inorder is left-node-right, postorder is left-right-node; iterative versions replace recursion with an explicit stack.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Preorder** – visit the node, then traverse the left subtree, then the right subtree (node-left-right).
- **Inorder** – traverse the left subtree, visit the node, then traverse the right subtree (left-node-right).
- **Postorder** – traverse both subtrees, then visit the node (left-right-node).
- **Recursive** – each traversal is a three-line method with a null base case.
- **Iterative** – an explicit `ArrayDeque` stack replaces the JVM call stack, preventing `StackOverflowError` on very tall trees.
- **BST property** – inorder on a binary search tree produces sorted output.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh audits the National Bank of India org chart three ways. In preorder he writes a manager's name first, then audits their teams. In inorder he audits the left team fully, writes the manager, then audits the right team. In postorder he audits both teams completely before writing the manager last. Same chart, three orders, chosen depending on what the audit needs.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Tree:        1
             /   \
            2     3
           / \
          4   5

  Preorder  (node-left-right): 1 → 2 → 4 → 5 → 3
  Inorder   (left-node-right): 4 → 2 → 5 → 1 → 3
  Postorder (left-right-node): 4 → 5 → 2 → 3 → 1
```

```text
  Iterative Inorder Stack Walk
  ────────────────────────────
  curr=1: push 1, go left
  curr=2: push 2, go left
  curr=4: push 4, go left
  curr=null: pop 4 → visit 4, go right (null)
  pop 2 → visit 2, go right (5)
  curr=5: push 5, go left (null)
  pop 5 → visit 5, go right (null)
  pop 1 → visit 1, go right (3)
  curr=3: push 3, go left (null)
  pop 3 → visit 3, go right (null)
  Stack empty + curr null → done

  Output: [4, 2, 5, 1, 3]
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The three depth-first traversals differ only in when the node is visited relative to its children. Preorder visits first, inorder visits between, and postorder visits last. The recursive forms are trivially clear, but the iterative forms matter in production because they avoid `StackOverflowError` on very tall trees by using an explicit heap-allocated stack.

Iterative preorder pushes root, pops and visits, then pushes right before left so left is processed first. Iterative inorder goes left pushing nodes, pops and visits, then moves right. Iterative postorder uses the reverse trick: run node-right-left and reverse the result to get left-right-node. All six versions are O(n) time and O(h) space.

The single most important property to remember is that inorder on a binary search tree yields sorted output. This makes inorder the natural traversal for BST validation, kth-smallest, and range queries. Recognizing this connection is what interviewers look for.

In my project at the National Bank of India, I used these on a fee expression tree. Preorder gave prefix export, inorder gave human-readable infix display, and postorder gave exactly the token order for the stack-based evaluator. The iterative versions ran in production to handle arbitrarily deep formula trees safely.

Remember one sentence: preorder is node-left-right, inorder is left-node-right, postorder is left-right-node, and the iterative versions replace the call stack with an explicit stack for safety.
